test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 18 Aug 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. You have to consider these statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, and decide which of the given conclusions logically follow/s from the given statements.

Statements:

All donkeys are zebras.

Some bulls are cats.

Some donkeys are apes.

Conclusions:

(I) Some zebras are bulls.

(II) Some zebras are apes.

(III) Some donkeys are cats.
solution:
**Given Statements:**

All donkeys are zebras.

Some bulls are cats.

Some donkeys are apes.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/77af12834fca622940059280ba9ed5c3ac13a2fc2d231248b1566edd531bf2ad.png] 

**Conclusions:**

(I) Some zebras are bulls → False (Because there is no relation given between zebras and bulls, so it can be possible but not definitely true)

(II) Some zebras are apes → **True** (Because it is given that some donkeys are apes and all donkeys are zebras, the part which is common in donkeys and apes is also zebra.)

(III) Some donkeys are cats → False (Because there is no relation given between donkeys and cats, so it can be possible but not definitely true)

So, only conclusion II follows.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3"**.
